template.name: GlobalClock
template.declaration:
/* * GlobalClock — the single real-valued clock in the entire NTA (variable c). * Role: converts continuous dense time into a discrete sequence of tick! broadcasts, exactly 1 time unit apart (Assumption 1: 1 time unit = 0.1 s). * Every other template reacts only to tick? and to bounded integer counters derived from it — this is the ONLY clock in the whole model, so the DBM/zone dimension stays * at 1 regardless of how many processes are composed, which is what keeps verification tractable given the number of moving-row instances. * Also fires timeOut! the instant globalTick reaches currentLevelTimeLimit, then resets both the clock and the tick counter for the next attempt. */
clock c;

location.name: Running
location.label: c <= 1

GlobalClock — the single real-valued clock in the entire NTA (variable c). Role: converts continuous dense time into a discrete sequence of tick! broadcasts, exactly 1 time unit apart (Assumption 1: 1 time unit = 0.1 s). Every other template reacts only to tick? and to bounded integer counters derived from it — this is the ONLY clock in the whole model, so the DBM/zone dimension stays at 1 regardless of how many processes are composed, which is what keeps verification tractable given the number of moving-row instances. Also fires timeOut! the instant globalTick reaches currentLevelTimeLimit, then resets both the clock and the tick counter for the next attempt.

location.name: Start
location.label: GameManager — owns the meta-game state: lives, score, and the overall attempt lifecycle (Start -> WaitingRespawn -> Playing -> WaitingRespawn -> ...). Role: reacts to reachBay? (award points, and on all-bays-occupied, complete the level), loseOneLife? and timeOut? (decrement a life and reset the attempt). frogMoveTimer enforces the "Frogger may move again only 2 seconds after death or a bay reach" rule (2s = 20 time units at 0.1s/unit): it counts ticks while in WaitingRespawn and only fires frogInitPosition! once the threshold is reached. WaitingRespawn intentionally spans many ticks (real waiting) and is therefore NOT a committed location, unlike the short-lived signalling locations elsewhere.

template.name: RowRoad

location.name: Running
location.label: RowRoad — parametrised template, one instance per moving row (vehicles, logs, turtles); id selects which row of the const rowInfo[] table this instance drives. Role: on every tick?, updateRow(id) checks whether this row's movement period has elapsed (globalTick % speed == 0) and, if so, shifts every object in the row by one cell via moveRow(id), wrapping around using TOTAL_LOOP (= WIDTH + BORDER_DELAY) to reproduce the "reappear after traversing two extra cells" rule. Per the assignment's hint, object positions are NEVER reset once the game starts — they are relative shifts, so they keep moving continuously even when globalTick resets on respawn/level-complete. The single Running location persists for the whole game; it is not committed, since real time must elapse here between shifts.

location.name: AboveWater
location.label: DivingTurtle — single shared process controlling the isSubmerged flag used by BOTH diving-turtle groups (row 7 and row 10); modeled once rather than duplicated, since no required property depends on the two groups submerging independently. Role: abstracts the manual's 4-phase cycle (emerged -> diving -> submerged -> emerging, 10/5/10/5 time units) into a 2-location model (AboveWater/Submerged) with combined thresholds, since only "can Frogger safely stand here" (AboveWater) vs. "does Frogger die" (Submerged) is observable by the rest of the system. timer counts ticks within the current phase and is reset on each transition.

template.name: Frogger

location.name: Respawning
location.label: Frogger — the player-controlled process; owns frog_x/frog_y and all collision logic. Role: on tick?, attempts to move up one cell (moveFrog) if canMoveUp() allows it (map boundary and target-home-bay-must-be-free checks), then immediately evaluates the outcome in EvaluateSafety: checkCollision() determines death on road/river rows via getObjectAtPosition()/isCellOccupied() (which floating-object or vehicle group, if any, currently occupies the frog's cell), while reaching a HOME row triggers reachBay! and occupyHomeBay(). EvaluateSafety is committed: the collision/home-bay decision must be resolved atomically, before any RowRoad instance advances again or GameManager reacts to a stale board state — this is the canonical "compute-then-branch, zero elapsed time" case committed locations exist for. Playing and Respawning are plain locations, since both persist across many ticks while waiting for the next event.
